    Potential production (winter wheat)¶

    This example runs torchcrop's Lintul5 model in potential production mode over nineteen winter-wheat growing seasons (1972-1990 sowing years) at West Lafayette, Indiana, then plots the full state and diagnostic trajectories of each season against development stage (DVS).

    Potential production is the model's highest-yielding mode: crop growth is driven only by the weather (solar radiation and temperature) and the crop's phenological development. There is no water, nitrogen, phosphorus or potassium limitation — every stress reduction factor stays at 1, so the resulting yield is the upper bound achievable under the given weather. It is configured with two switches:

    Switch Value Effect
    crop_params.iopt 1 Run mode = potential → nutrient stress switched off
    soil_params.irri 1 Automatic irrigation → soil water kept non-limiting

    Unlike the Brandenburg reference set (18 distinct locations, all sown on the same calendar day), Indiana's actual sowing date shifts from year to year, so here each "location" is one sowing season — the same site, but a different IDPL (sowing day-of-year) per year. Each season's weather file starts 1 January of the sowing year and runs a fixed 570 days into the following year (long enough for autumn sowing to reach maturity), so the model is driven with start_doy=1 and relies on its internal sowing latch for the pre-sowing spin-up, exactly as with a single static IDPL.

    Prepare dataset and dataloader¶

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    class TorchCropDataset(Dataset):
    """Reads per-location weather, soil, and site data for torchcrop.

    Directory layout (under ``DATA_DIR``)::

        weather/<location>.csv   daily forcing, one file per location
        soil/soil.csv            one row per location, indexed by ``location``
        site/site.csv            one row per location, indexed by ``location``

    Here each "location" is actually one **sowing season** (keyed by sowing
    year) at the same West Lafayette site, since Indiana's winter-wheat
    sowing date shifts year to year -- unlike the Brandenburg reference set,
    where each location is a distinct place sown on the same calendar date.
    Each season's weather file spans a fixed-length window starting 1
    January of the sowing year and running long enough into the following
    year to reach maturity, and each site.csv row carries that season's own
    ``IDPL``.

    ``__getitem__`` returns a single sample as a dict with:

        * ``weather`` : ``[T, 8]`` float tensor in torchcrop channel order
          (DOY, davtmp, tmin, tmax, irrad, rain, vp, wind)
        * ``soil``    : dict of scalar floats keyed by ``SoilParameters`` field
        * ``site``    : dict of scalar floats keyed by ``SiteParameters`` field

    Use `collate_torchcrop` as the DataLoader ``collate_fn`` to assemble a
    batch into ready-to-run ``WeatherDriver`` / ``SoilParameters`` /
    ``SiteParameters`` objects.
    """

    # CSV weather columns, in the exact order torchcrop expects them.
    WEATHER_COLS = [
        "Date",          # -> doy
        "TempMean",      # -> davtmp (recomputed as (TempMin+TempMax)/2 below)
        "TempMin",       # -> tmin
        "TempMax",       # -> tmax
        "Radiation",     # -> irrad
        "Precipitation", # -> rain
        "VapPressure",   # -> vp
        "Windspeed",     # -> wind
    ]

    # soil.csv column -> SoilParameters field name
    SOIL_MAP = {
        "SMDRY": "wcad",       # air-dry volumetric water content [m³ m⁻³]
        "SMW": "wcwp",         # water content at wilting point [m³ m⁻³]
        "SMFC": "wcfc",        # water content at field capacity [m³ m⁻³]
        "SMO": "wcst",         # water content at saturation [m³ m⁻³]
        "CRAIRC": "crairc",    # critical air content for aeration [m³ m⁻³]
        "SMI": "wci",          # initial root-zone moisture content [m³ m⁻³]
        "SMLOWI": "wci_lower", # initial lower-zone (sub-soil) moisture [m³ m⁻³]
        "RDMSO": "rdmso",      # max rooting depth allowed by the soil [m]
        "RUNFR": "runfr",      # fraction of rainfall lost to surface runoff [0–1]
        "CFEV": "cfev",        # soil-evaporation correction factor [-] (1–4)
        "KSUB": "ksub",        # max percolation rate to deeper layers [mm d⁻¹]
        "NMINS": "nmini",      # initial mineralisable soil organic N [g N m⁻²]
        "PMINS": "pmini",      # initial mineralisable soil organic P [g P m⁻²]
        "KMINS": "kmini",      # initial mineralisable soil organic K [g K m⁻²]
        "RTNMINS": "rtnmins",  # daily N mineralisation fraction [d⁻¹]
        "RTPMINS": "rtpmins",  # daily P mineralisation fraction [d⁻¹]
        "RTKMINS": "rtkmins",  # daily K mineralisation fraction [d⁻¹]
    }

    # site.csv column -> SiteParameters field name
    SITE_MAP = {
        "LATITUDE": "latitude",
        "ALTITUDE": "altitude",
        "IDPL": "idpl",
        "CO2": "co2",
    }

    def __init__(self, weather_dir, soil_dir, site_dir, dtype=torch.float32):
        super().__init__()
        self.weather_dir = Path(weather_dir)
        self.dtype = dtype
        self.soil_data = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(soil_dir, "soil.csv")).set_index("location")
        self.site_data = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(site_dir, "site.csv")).set_index("location")
        # Locations present in both soil and site tables.
        self.locations = self.soil_data.index.intersection(self.site_data.index)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.locations)

    def _load_weather(self, location):
        df = pd.read_csv(self.weather_dir / f"{location}.csv", parse_dates=["Date"], dayfirst=True)
        df = df[self.WEATHER_COLS].copy()
        # SIMPLACE drives phenology with TMPA = (TMIN+TMAX)/2 (Phenology.java:513),
        # not the measured TempMean; match it to reproduce the reference.
        df["TempMean"] = (df["TempMin"] + df["TempMax"]) / 2.0
        df["Radiation"] = df["Radiation"] / 1000.0   # kJ -> MJ m-2 d-1
        df["Date"] = df["Date"].dt.dayofyear          # date -> day-of-year
        return torch.as_tensor(df.values, dtype=self.dtype)  # [T, 8]

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        location = self.locations[idx]

        weather = self._load_weather(location)

        srow = self.soil_data.loc[location]
        soil = {field: float(srow[col]) for col, field in self.SOIL_MAP.items()}

        trow = self.site_data.loc[location]
        site = {field: float(trow[col]) for col, field in self.SITE_MAP.items()}

        return {"weather": weather, "soil": soil, "site": site}


def collate_torchcrop(batch, dtype=torch.float32):
    """Collate samples into batched torchcrop driver/parameter objects.

    Args:
        batch: list of samples produced by `TorchCropDataset.__getitem__`.
        dtype: target dtype for the assembled tensors.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(weather, soil_params, site_params)`` where ``weather`` is a
        `WeatherDriver` of shape ``[B, T, 8]`` and ``soil_params`` /
        ``site_params`` are batched dataclasses with ``[B]`` scalar fields.
    """
    # Weather: [B, T, 8]
    weather = torch.stack([s["weather"] for s in batch], dim=0).to(dtype)
    weather = WeatherDriver(weather)

    # Soil / site: stack each field across the batch into a [B] tensor.
    soil_fields = batch[0]["soil"].keys()
    soil_kwargs = {
        f: torch.tensor([s["soil"][f] for s in batch], dtype=dtype)
        for f in soil_fields
    }
    soil_params = SoilParameters(**soil_kwargs)

    site_fields = batch[0]["site"].keys()
    site_kwargs = {
        f: torch.tensor([s["site"][f] for s in batch], dtype=dtype)
        for f in site_fields
    }
    site_params = SiteParameters(**site_kwargs)

    return weather, soil_params, site_params

    Run the model — potential production (no water or nutrient stress)¶

    The production level is controlled by two switches:

    • crop_params.iopt — the crop run mode:
    iopt Mode
    1 Potential (no stress)
    2 Water-limited
    3 Water + N limited
    4 Water + N + P + K limited
    • soil_params.irri — the irrigation mode (0 = rain-fed, 1 = automatic refill to field capacity, 2 = scheduled table).

    For potential production we set iopt = 1 (nutrients non-limiting) and irri = 1 (automatic irrigation), so both the nutrient stress index and the water-stress factor TRANRF stay at 1 throughout the growing season.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    # Winter-wheat crop parameters in potential mode (IOPT=1): nutrient stress is switched off.
crop_params = CropParameters(crop_name="wheat")
crop_params.iopt = torch.tensor(1.0)

# Runtime override (not a package edit): the "wheat" preset's default TSUM2=1000
# (anthesis->maturity thermal sum) reaches DVS=2 before some seasons' septoria
# reference observations end -- 1980 by 8 days, 1984 by 17 days (see
# probe_tsum2.py). TSUM2=1450 was picked by probing candidate values against
# every season's last reference observation date; it's the smallest value in
# that sweep for which every season's simulated maturity is at or after its
# last reference date (1984 is the tightest, now 5 days past instead of 17
# short). Raising it delays maturity in all six seasons, not just the two that
# were short -- harmless (the extra days just have no reference to compare
# against) but it does shift every season's simulated yield/AGB.
crop_params.tsum1 = torch.tensor(1651.0)
crop_params.tsum2 = torch.tensor(614.0)

# Assemble every location (one per sowing season) into one batch and run a single forward pass.
samples = [dataset[i] for i in range(len(dataset))]
weather, soil_params, site_params = collate_torchcrop(samples)

# Automatic irrigation (IRRI=1): the root zone is refilled to field capacity,
# so soil water never limits growth and TRANRF stays at 1 (potential water supply)
soil_params.irri = torch.tensor(1.0)

# Move every tensor input onto the target device.
crop_params = crop_params.to(device=device)
soil_params = soil_params.to(device=device)
site_params = site_params.to(device=device)
weather = weather.to(device=device)

model = Lintul5Model(crop_params, soil_params, site_params).eval().to(device)
with torch.no_grad():
    output = model(weather, start_doy=1)

# Per-location summary at maturity.
results = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "location": list(dataset.locations),
        "yield_g_m2": np.round(output.yield_.tolist(), 2),
        "adjusted_yield_g_m2": np.round(output.adjusted_yield.tolist(), 2),
        "max_lai": np.round(output.lai.max(dim=1).values.tolist(), 2),
        "final_dvs": output.dvs[:, -1].tolist(),
    }
)
results

TSUM2=1450 was picked by probing candidate values against # every season's last reference observation date; it's the smallest value in # that sweep for which every season's simulated maturity is at or after its # last reference date (1984 is the tightest, now 5 days past instead of 17 # short). Raising it delays maturity in all six seasons, not just the two that # were short -- harmless (the extra days just have no reference to compare # against) but it does shift every season's simulated yield/AGB. crop_params.tsum1 = torch.tensor(1651.0) crop_params.tsum2 = torch.tensor(614.0) # Assemble every location (one per sowing season) into one batch and run a single forward pass. samples = [dataset[i] for i in range(len(dataset))] weather, soil_params, site_params = collate_torchcrop(samples) # Automatic irrigation (IRRI=1): the root zone is refilled to field capacity, # so soil water never limits growth and TRANRF stays at 1 (potential water supply) soil_params.irri = torch.tensor(1.0) # Move every tensor input onto the target device. crop_params = crop_params.to(device=device) soil_params = soil_params.to(device=device) site_params = site_params.to(device=device) weather = weather.to(device=device) model = Lintul5Model(crop_params, soil_params, site_params).eval().to(device) with torch.no_grad(): output = model(weather, start_doy=1) # Per-location summary at maturity. results = pd.DataFrame( { "location": list(dataset.locations), "yield_g_m2": np.round(output.yield_.tolist(), 2), "adjusted_yield_g_m2": np.round(output.adjusted_yield.tolist(), 2), "max_lai": np.round(output.lai.max(dim=1).values.tolist(), 2), "final_dvs": output.dvs[:, -1].tolist(), } ) results

    Visualizing the results¶

    The model returns two per-day trajectories that we visualise the same way:

    • State variables — output.states, a list of ModelState holding the model's stored pools (biomass, LAI, soil water, nutrient pools, …).
    • Diagnostic variables — output.diagnostics, a list of DiagnosticState holding the intermediate fluxes and stress factors computed each day (TRANRF, RUE, partitioning fractions, transpiration, …).

    Each weather series starts on 1 January, but the crop is autumn-sown at that season's own IDPL (varies year to year — see site.csv); masking to the sowing latch makes every curve start at the day of sowing. The short near-vertical segment at DVS 0 is the sowing→emergence interval; DVS then climbs 0 → 1 (anthesis) → 2 (maturity).

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# Pick five random (reproducible) locations
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
selected_idx = rng.choice(len(dataset.locations), size=5, replace=False)
locations = [dataset.locations[i] for i in selected_idx]
n_loc = len(locations)
colors = [
    "#1f77b4",  # blue
    "#d62728",  # red
    "#2ca02c",  # green
    "#ff7f0e",  # orange
    "#9467bd",  # purple
]

def mask_until_dvs2(sown_mask, dvs_vals):
    """Boolean mask selecting sown days up to and including maturity (DVS >= 2).

    Args:
        sown_mask: ``[L]`` bool array, ``True`` once the crop is sown.
        dvs_vals:  ``[L]`` development-stage values.

    Returns:
        ``[L]`` bool mask: sown days with index <= the first day DVS reaches 2.
    """
    mature = np.where(dvs_vals >= 2.0)[0]
    cutoff = mature[0] if len(mature) else len(dvs_vals)
    return sown_mask & (np.arange(len(dvs_vals)) <= cutoff)


def plot_trajectories(traj, dvs, sown, field_names, meta, *, title, ncols=4):
    """Plot every channel of ``traj`` against DVS, one line per location.

    A single helper used for both state and diagnostic figures so they share
    the same style, grid layout, labelling and legend.

    Args:
        traj:        ``[B, L, C]`` stacked trajectory array.
        dvs:         ``[B, L]`` development stage (x-axis).
        sown:        ``[B, L]`` sowing latch (> 0 once sown).
        field_names: length-``C`` list naming the channels of ``traj``.
        meta:        ``{field: (label, unit)}`` used for the panel titles.
        title:       figure super-title.
        ncols:       number of subplot columns.
    """
    nrows = int(np.ceil(len(field_names) / ncols))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=(4.2 * ncols, 2.4 * nrows), sharex=True)
    axes = axes.ravel()

    for ax, fld in zip(axes, field_names):
        j = field_names.index(fld)
        for c, b in enumerate(selected_idx):
            mask = mask_until_dvs2(sown[b] > 0, dvs[b])
            ax.plot(dvs[b][mask], traj[b, mask, j], color=colors[c], lw=1.2, alpha=0.9)
        label, unit = meta.get(fld, (fld, ""))
        ax.set_title(f"{label} [{unit}]" if unit else label, fontsize=11)
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
        ax.margins(x=0.02)

    # Hide unused panels; label the x-axis on the bottom row of plotted panels.
    for ax in axes[len(field_names):]:
        ax.axis("off")
    for ax in axes[max(0, len(field_names) - ncols):len(field_names)]:
        ax.set_xlabel("DVS")

    handles = [Line2D([0], [0], color=colors[i], lw=2) for i in range(n_loc)]
    fig.legend(
        handles,
        [str(loc) for loc in locations],
        title="Location",
        loc="lower center",
        ncol=n_loc,
        fontsize=12,
        bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.01),
        frameon=False,
    )
    fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=13)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.04, 1, 0.99])
    plt.show()
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D # Pick five random (reproducible) locations rng = np.random.default_rng(42) selected_idx = rng.choice(len(dataset.locations), size=5, replace=False) locations = [dataset.locations[i] for i in selected_idx] n_loc = len(locations) colors = [ "#1f77b4", # blue "#d62728", # red "#2ca02c", # green "#ff7f0e", # orange "#9467bd", # purple ] def mask_until_dvs2(sown_mask, dvs_vals): """Boolean mask selecting sown days up to and including maturity (DVS >= 2). Args: sown_mask: ``[L]`` bool array, ``True`` once the crop is sown. dvs_vals: ``[L]`` development-stage values. Returns: ``[L]`` bool mask: sown days with index <= the first day DVS reaches 2. """ mature = np.where(dvs_vals >= 2.0)[0] cutoff = mature[0] if len(mature) else len(dvs_vals) return sown_mask & (np.arange(len(dvs_vals)) <= cutoff) def plot_trajectories(traj, dvs, sown, field_names, meta, *, title, ncols=4): """Plot every channel of ``traj`` against DVS, one line per location. A single helper used for both state and diagnostic figures so they share the same style, grid layout, labelling and legend. Args: traj: ``[B, L, C]`` stacked trajectory array. dvs: ``[B, L]`` development stage (x-axis). sown: ``[B, L]`` sowing latch (> 0 once sown). field_names: length-``C`` list naming the channels of ``traj``. meta: ``{field: (label, unit)}`` used for the panel titles. title: figure super-title. ncols: number of subplot columns. """ nrows = int(np.ceil(len(field_names) / ncols)) fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=(4.2 * ncols, 2.4 * nrows), sharex=True) axes = axes.ravel() for ax, fld in zip(axes, field_names): j = field_names.index(fld) for c, b in enumerate(selected_idx): mask = mask_until_dvs2(sown[b] > 0, dvs[b]) ax.plot(dvs[b][mask], traj[b, mask, j], color=colors[c], lw=1.2, alpha=0.9) label, unit = meta.get(fld, (fld, "")) ax.set_title(f"{label} [{unit}]" if unit else label, fontsize=11) ax.grid(alpha=0.3) ax.margins(x=0.02) # Hide unused panels; label the x-axis on the bottom row of plotted panels. for ax in axes[len(field_names):]: ax.axis("off") for ax in axes[max(0, len(field_names) - ncols):len(field_names)]: ax.set_xlabel("DVS") handles = [Line2D([0], [0], color=colors[i], lw=2) for i in range(n_loc)] fig.legend( handles, [str(loc) for loc in locations], title="Location", loc="lower center", ncol=n_loc, fontsize=12, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.01), frameon=False, ) fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=13) fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.04, 1, 0.99]) plt.show()

    6. Feed the torchcrop run into FraNchEstYN (septoria + fungicide)¶

    torchcrop simulates crop growth only — no pest, disease, or fungicide effects. simpest.models.franchestyn layers a septoria SEIR epidemic and a fungicide-efficacy model on top of an external attainable crop-growth trajectory (light interception, biomass, yield, thermal time), then reports the actual (disease-limited) trajectory. The nineteen seasons already run above supply that attainable trajectory; the cells below convert torchcrop's in-memory tensors into the three DataFrames run_franchestyn expects (weather_df, management_df, crop_model_df), matching the column contracts in simpest/models/fr_weather_reader.py, fr_reference_reader.py, and fr_data.py.

    Reference septoria-severity observations for this same West Lafayette site are reused from docs/examples/data/reference_fra/FRA_REFERENCE_Indiana.csv (1973–1991) to calibrate the disease parameters — this run's torchcrop-driven crop growth is independent of that file's origin, only the location and disease-observation years need to line up with our 1972–1991 window.

    In [9]:

    # Helper lambdas, same pattern as 3_TorchCropIntegration.ipynb: pull a named
# field out of the stacked trajectories -> [B, T] numpy, end-of-day aligned.
def sf(field):
    return state_traj[:, 1:, field_names.index(field)]

def df_(field):
    return diag_traj[:, :, diag_field_names.index(field)]

# torchcrop -> FraNchEstYN unit bridge. torchcrop's biomass states are g m-2, (torchcrop/states/model_state.py); 
# FraNchEstYN's CropModelData.agb/.yield_ contract is kg ha-1 (simpest/models/fr_data.py). 1 g/m2 = 10 kg/ha.
G_M2_TO_KG_HA = 10.0

agb_all   = (sf("wlv") + sf("wlvd") + sf("wst") + sf("wstd") + sf("wso")) * G_M2_TO_KG_HA
yield_all = sf("wso") * G_M2_TO_KG_HA
gdd_all   = sf("tsum")               # thermal time since emergence, torchcrop's analogue of SIMPLACE TSUM
fint_all  = df_("frac_intercepted")


# For each season, take sowing day -> first day DVS reaches 2 (maturity), then concatenate every season into one multi-year series.
rows = []
for b, sow_year in enumerate(dataset.locations):
    idpl = int(dataset.site_data.loc[sow_year, "IDPL"])
    sow_idx = idpl - 1   # day 0 = 1 January of sow_year
    maturity_idx = np.where(dvs_traj[b, 1:] >= 2.0)[0][0]

    dates = pd.Timestamp(year=int(sow_year), month=1, day=1) + pd.to_timedelta(np.arange(sow_idx, maturity_idx + 1), unit="D")
    rows.append(pd.DataFrame({
        "year":   dates.year,
        "doy":    dates.dayofyear,
        "agb":    agb_all[b, sow_idx : maturity_idx + 1],
        "yield":  yield_all[b, sow_idx : maturity_idx + 1],
        "fint":   fint_all[b, sow_idx : maturity_idx + 1],
        "gdd":    gdd_all[b, sow_idx : maturity_idx + 1],
        "season": int(sow_year),
    }))

crop_model_df = pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True).sort_values(["year", "doy"]).reset_index(drop=True)
print(crop_model_df.tail())
    # Helper lambdas, same pattern as 3_TorchCropIntegration.ipynb: pull a named # field out of the stacked trajectories -> [B, T] numpy, end-of-day aligned. def sf(field): return state_traj[:, 1:, field_names.index(field)] def df_(field): return diag_traj[:, :, diag_field_names.index(field)] # torchcrop -> FraNchEstYN unit bridge. torchcrop's biomass states are g m-2, (torchcrop/states/model_state.py); # FraNchEstYN's CropModelData.agb/.yield_ contract is kg ha-1 (simpest/models/fr_data.py). 1 g/m2 = 10 kg/ha. G_M2_TO_KG_HA = 10.0 agb_all = (sf("wlv") + sf("wlvd") + sf("wst") + sf("wstd") + sf("wso")) * G_M2_TO_KG_HA yield_all = sf("wso") * G_M2_TO_KG_HA gdd_all = sf("tsum") # thermal time since emergence, torchcrop's analogue of SIMPLACE TSUM fint_all = df_("frac_intercepted") # For each season, take sowing day -> first day DVS reaches 2 (maturity), then concatenate every season into one multi-year series. rows = [] for b, sow_year in enumerate(dataset.locations): idpl = int(dataset.site_data.loc[sow_year, "IDPL"]) sow_idx = idpl - 1 # day 0 = 1 January of sow_year maturity_idx = np.where(dvs_traj[b, 1:] >= 2.0)[0][0] dates = pd.Timestamp(year=int(sow_year), month=1, day=1) + pd.to_timedelta(np.arange(sow_idx, maturity_idx + 1), unit="D") rows.append(pd.DataFrame({ "year": dates.year, "doy": dates.dayofyear, "agb": agb_all[b, sow_idx : maturity_idx + 1], "yield": yield_all[b, sow_idx : maturity_idx + 1], "fint": fint_all[b, sow_idx : maturity_idx + 1], "gdd": gdd_all[b, sow_idx : maturity_idx + 1], "season": int(sow_year), })) crop_model_df = pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True).sort_values(["year", "doy"]).reset_index(drop=True) print(crop_model_df.tail())

# Damage-coefficient params excluded from calibration (cannot be identified from severity data alone).
damage_disable = {"RUEreducerDamage", "LightStealerDamage", "SenescenceAcceleratorDamage", "AssimilateSappersDamage",}
fr_cfg.disease_parameters = franchestyn.deactivate_calibration(fr_cfg.disease_parameters, damage_disable)

# Mechanistic groups, in dependency order (see notebook discussion): C (cardinal
# temperatures) feeds both B's hourly infection-efficiency calc and A's
# latency/sporulation GDD progress; B's accumulated hydrothermal-time state
# feeds A's onset gate; D (inoculum/spread magnitude) is a pure scale on top
# of A+B+C, so it's calibrated last.
GROUPS = [
    ("A: onset & cycle timing", {"HydroThermalTimeOnset", "CyclePercentageOnset", "LatencyDuration", "SporulationDuration",}),
    ("B: environmental infection-trigger", {"WetnessDurationOptimum", "WetnessDurationMinimum", "DryCriticalInterruption","RelativeHumidityCritical", "RelativeHumidityNotLimiting", "Rain50Detachment",}),
    ("C: temperature response", {"Tmin", "Topt", "Tmax"}),
    ("D: inoculum & spread magnitude", {"OuterInoculumMax", "OuterInoculumShapeParameter", "PathogenSpread",}),
]

    def set_active_group(active_names):
    """calibration=True only for active_names; every other (non-damage) param
    stays fixed at its current 'value'."""
    all_names = set(fr_cfg.disease_parameters) - damage_disable
    franchestyn.deactivate_calibration(fr_cfg.disease_parameters, all_names - active_names)
    for name in active_names:
        fr_cfg.disease_parameters[name]["calibration"] = True

def run_franchestyn_now():
    return franchestyn.run_franchestyn(
        weather_df=weather_df, management_df=management_df, crop_model_df=crop_model_df,
        ref_df=ref_df, start_year=FRANCH_START_YEAR, end_year=FRANCH_END_YEAR, config=fr_cfg,
    )


def run_stage(active_names, n_restarts=2, max_iter=50):
    set_active_group(active_names)
    fr_cfg.is_calibration = True
    fr_cfg.n_restarts = n_restarts
    fr_cfg.max_iter = max_iter
    result = run_franchestyn_now()
    rmse = result["outputs"]["summary"]["rmse"]
    fitted = {k.split("_", 1)[1]: v for k, v in result["outputs"]["summary"]["best_params"].items()}
    return fitted, rmse


def run_forward():
    """Full-model RMSE with every parameter held at its current fixed 'value'."""
    was_calib = fr_cfg.is_calibration
    fr_cfg.is_calibration = False
    result = run_franchestyn_now()
    fr_cfg.is_calibration = was_calib
    return result

    Parameter sensitivity screen (Morris)¶

    run_morris_sensitivity uses the same parameter selection as calibration (flagged for calibration, disease scope, damage parameters excluded) and the same RMSE objective. Cost is about n_trajectories * (k + 1) model runs.

    • mu_star - mean absolute effect on the severity RMSE. Higher = more influential.
    • sigma - spread of the effects. High relative to mu_star = non-linear or interacting with other parameters.
    • mu_star_conf - bootstrap confidence interval on mu_star.

    import copy

MAX_SWEEPS = 4
TOL = 0.5  # stop once a sweep improves RMSE by less than this many points

sweep_rmse = [run_forward()["outputs"]["summary"]["rmse"]]
print(f"Starting RMSE (all defaults): {sweep_rmse[0]:.3f}")

for sweep in range(MAX_SWEEPS):
    print(f"\n=== Sweep {sweep + 1}/{MAX_SWEEPS} ===")
    snapshot = copy.deepcopy(fr_cfg.disease_parameters)

    for group_name, names in GROUPS:
        fitted, rmse = run_stage(names)
        print(f"  {group_name}: RMSE={rmse:.2f}")
        for p in names:
            fr_cfg.disease_parameters[p]["value"] = float(fitted[p])

    full_rmse = run_forward()["outputs"]["summary"]["rmse"]
    print(f"Sweep {sweep + 1} full-model RMSE: {full_rmse:.3f}")

    if full_rmse > sweep_rmse[-1]:
        print("Sweep made things worse -- reverting to the previous sweep's parameters.")
        fr_cfg.disease_parameters = snapshot
        break
    sweep_rmse.append(full_rmse)
    if sweep_rmse[-2] - sweep_rmse[-1] < TOL:
        print("Converged (improvement below tolerance).")
        break

print("\nSweep RMSE history:", [round(r, 2) for r in sweep_rmse])

    # Final joint polish: re-enable every parameter and calibrate them together.
active_names = set().union(*(names for _, names in GROUPS))
for p in active_names:
    fr_cfg.disease_parameters[p]["calibration"] = True

fr_cfg.is_calibration = True
fr_cfg.n_restarts = 3
fr_cfg.max_iter = 100
result = run_franchestyn_now()

summary = result["outputs"]["summary"]
simulation_df = pd.DataFrame(result["outputs"]["simulation"])
simulation_df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(simulation_df["Date"], dayfirst=True)

season_summary = franchestyn.build_season_summary(simulation_df, site=fr_cfg.site, variety=fr_cfg.variety)

# FraNchEstYN stores disease severity as a 0-1 fraction internally;
# build_season_summary expects that and multiplies by 100 for AUDPC, so
# convert to percent only after the summary is built.
simulation_df["DiseaseSeverity"] = simulation_df["DiseaseSeverity"] * 100.0
season_summary["DiseaseSeverity"] = season_summary["DiseaseSeverity"] * 100.0

print("FraNchEstYN completed")
print("RMSE (disease severity vs reference):", summary.get("rmse"))
print(f"{len(season_summary)} growing seasons summarised")
season_summary

    n_seasons = len(dataset.locations)
n_cols = 7
n_rows = int(np.ceil(n_seasons / n_cols))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, n_cols, figsize=(28, 3.5 * n_rows), sharey=True)
axes_flat = axes.ravel()
ref_dis = ref_df[ref_df[FRANCH_DISEASE].notna()]

for i, sow_year in enumerate(dataset.locations):
    ax = axes_flat[i]
    harvest_yr = sow_year + 1
    sub = simulation_df[simulation_df["GrowingSeason"] == sow_year]
    ax.plot(sub["Date"], sub["DiseaseSeverity"], color="tab:red", lw=1.2, label="Simulated")

    ref_yr = ref_dis[ref_dis["year"] == harvest_yr]
    if not ref_yr.empty:
        ref_dates = pd.Timestamp(year=harvest_yr, month=1, day=1) + pd.to_timedelta(ref_yr["DOY"] - 1, unit="D")
        ax.scatter(ref_dates, ref_yr[FRANCH_DISEASE], color="darkred", s=20, zorder=5, label="Observed")

    ax.set_title(f"{sow_year}/{str(harvest_yr)[2:]}", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlim(pd.Timestamp(f"{harvest_yr}-01-01"), pd.Timestamp(f"{harvest_yr}-12-31"))
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(plt.matplotlib.dates.MonthLocator(bymonth=[1, 4, 7, 10]))
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.matplotlib.dates.DateFormatter("%b"))
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=8, rotation=45)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

# Hide any unused panels (n_seasons may not fill the grid exactly).
for ax in axes_flat[n_seasons:]:
    ax.axis("off")

handles, labels = axes_flat[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
fig.legend(handles, labels, loc="lower center", ncol=2, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.01))
fig.supylabel("Septoria severity [%]")
fig.suptitle("torchcrop-driven crop growth + FraNchEstYN septoria: simulated vs observed", fontsize=12)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

for i, sow_year in enumerate(dataset.locations):

    ax.plot(sub["Date"], sub["RHx"], color="tab:blue", lw=1.0, label="RHx (max)")
    ax.plot(sub["Date"], sub["RHn"], color="tab:orange", lw=1.0, label="RHn (min)")

    ax.set_title(f"{sow_year}/{str(harvest_yr)[2:]}", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlim(pd.Timestamp(f"{harvest_yr}-01-01"), pd.Timestamp(f"{harvest_yr}-12-31"))
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(plt.matplotlib.dates.MonthLocator(bymonth=[1, 4, 7, 10]))
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.matplotlib.dates.DateFormatter("%b"))
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=8, rotation=45)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

# Hide any unused panels (n_seasons may not fill the grid exactly).
for ax in axes_flat[n_seasons:]:
    ax.axis("off")

handles, labels = axes_flat[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
fig.legend(handles, labels, loc="lower center", ncol=2, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.01))
fig.supylabel("Relative humidity [%]")
fig.suptitle("Daily relative humidity extremes (RHx/RHn) per season", fontsize=12)
fig.tight_layout()

    7. Error diagnostics: simulated vs observed¶

    At every reference observation date (severity from thisDisease, canopy closure from FINT), match the simulated value on that same calendar date and take the residual simulated - observed. A parity plot shows overall bias/spread against the 1:1 line; the residual-over-time plot shows whether errors cluster in a particular part of the season (color marks over- vs under-prediction).

    Copied! 
    def match_ref_to_sim(ref_col, sim_col, sim_scale=1.0):
    """Match reference observations to same-date simulated values, per season."""
    rows = []
    for sow_year in dataset.locations:
        harvest_yr = sow_year + 1
        sub = simulation_df[simulation_df["GrowingSeason"] == sow_year].set_index("Date")
        ref_sub = ref_df[(ref_df["year"] == harvest_yr) & ref_df[ref_col].notna()]
        if ref_sub.empty:
            continue
        ref_dates = pd.Timestamp(year=harvest_yr, month=1, day=1) + pd.to_timedelta(ref_sub["DOY"] - 1, unit="D")
        for date, obs in zip(ref_dates, ref_sub[ref_col]):
            if date in sub.index:
                rows.append({
                    "season": sow_year,
                    "date": date,
                    "observed": obs,
                    "simulated": sub.loc[date, sim_col] * sim_scale,
                })
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out["error"] = out["simulated"] - out["observed"]
    return out

severity_err = match_ref_to_sim(FRANCH_DISEASE, "DiseaseSeverity")
fint_err = match_ref_to_sim("FINT", "LightInterception")

print(f"severity: n={len(severity_err)}  RMSE={np.sqrt((severity_err['error']**2).mean()):.2f}  MAE={severity_err['error'].abs().mean():.2f}")
print(f"fint:     n={len(fint_err)}  RMSE={np.sqrt((fint_err['error']**2).mean()):.3f}  MAE={fint_err['error'].abs().mean():.3f}")

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(28, 8))

panels = [(severity_err, "Septoria severity", "%"), (fint_err, "Light interception (FINT)", "[-]")]
for row, (err_df, label, unit) in enumerate(panels):
    ax_parity, ax_resid = axes[row]

    lo, hi = 0, max(err_df["observed"].max(), err_df["simulated"].max()) * 1.05
    ax_parity.plot([lo, hi], [lo, hi], color="0.6", lw=1, ls="--", zorder=1)
    ax_parity.scatter(err_df["observed"], err_df["simulated"], s=28, color="tab:blue", edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.4, zorder=2)
    ax_parity.set_xlim(lo, hi)
    ax_parity.set_ylim(lo, hi)
    ax_parity.set_aspect("equal")
    ax_parity.set_xlabel(f"Observed [{unit}]")
    ax_parity.set_ylabel(f"Simulated [{unit}]")
    ax_parity.set_title(f"{label}: parity")
    ax_parity.grid(alpha=0.3)

    err_colors = np.where(err_df["error"] >= 0, "tab:red", "tab:blue")
    ax_resid.axhline(0, color="0.6", lw=1, ls="--", zorder=1)
    ax_resid.scatter(err_df["date"], err_df["error"], s=28, color=err_colors, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.4, zorder=2)
    ax_resid.set_xlabel("Date")
    ax_resid.set_ylabel(f"Error, sim - obs [{unit}]")
    ax_resid.set_title(f"{label}: residuals over time")
    ax_resid.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45, labelsize=8)
    ax_resid.grid(alpha=0.3)

    rmse = np.sqrt((err_df["error"] ** 2).mean())
    mae = err_df["error"].abs().mean()
    ax_resid.text(0.02, 0.95, f"RMSE={rmse:.2f}  MAE={mae:.2f}  n={len(err_df)}",
                  transform=ax_resid.transAxes, fontsize=8, va="top")

    Peak severity vs weather drivers¶

    The error diagnostics above show season-to-season range compression: the model's peak severity per season varies far less than the observed peaks do, even though the two are moderately correlated. Check which weather driver the real season-to-season swings track most closely, and whether the simulated peaks track it as well.
